**《边市律令适用与司法框架》要点（廷尉府拟）**

一、律令分层。凡谋反、谋叛、通敌、劫盗杀伤等刑律重罪，及军法、官制、符传关禁，一断于中央律，该城不得擅立。其市易、契约、质剂、度量衡、商贾争讼，许该城因时地之宜补律立令，然不得与中央律相抵牾。

二、备案审查。地方诸令颁行前须先上廷尉备案，廷尉三十日内核之；与中央律相抵或有害法统者，驳之。未经备案或已遭驳斥者，不得施行。已行之令，廷尉亦得追审废之。

《边镇互市关税与财政制度》要点（治粟内史上呈）

**一、税率浮动带**
诸税以治粟内史核定基准为则，许镇于带内自调：过税（关税）升降毋得过二成，市税毋得过三成。旺市减以招商，淡市增以保课，岁中可二调。凡调整须先报内史备案；逾带者以越权论。

**二、岁入分成，按税种分账**
过税归中央七成、留镇三成；市税中央四成、镇六成；盐铁之利尽归中央，镇给一成作护送转输之费。岁入超额，溢额六四分之；短额由镇自行补足。分成比例三岁一校，视贸易盈绌更定。

**三、铸币、度量衡皆中央专权**
钱式、币制、权衡、斗斛、尺丈一依秦律，镇不得私铸、改式、增减。违者以盗铸论罪。

**四、账册制度**
设双重之籍：镇存一册，月录副本上郡与治粟内史；季汇岁考。中央遣吏核账，验货与籍相合；隐匿、虚报、漏籍者坐之。

**五、禁绝战略物资资敌**
军械、甲胄、弩机、铁器、逾额之粮、战马严禁出关，不得享任何减免优例。关市验传验货并行，商贾必持符传；告发私运者赏没值之半，纵容之吏并坐。

**六、财政触发条款**
有下列其一，即撤自治，镇吏下廷尉：
1. 连续两季亏欠应上缴之额；
2. 账实差逾一成而无正解；
3. 禁物走私案发而回护不举；
4. 逾带擅调税率或私设杂税；
5. 擅自借贷、私储军粮兵器、私募兵卒。

《防务与反间安排》要点

一、驻军体制
本镇常备驻军由中央调发，直属太尉节制，主将由朝廷除授，非经虎符验合不得发兵。兵权专属驻军主将，城防、治安各员不得干预调遣。商人议事会仅议商事、市规与赋税分摊，**兵权绝不假借**；凡议事会人员不得入军幕、阅军籍、督操练。

二、本地治安力量
城得设亭长、捕盗吏及市卒，总额限三百人以内，著于郡籍。器械止于木梃、短兵、轻弓，**不得披甲、持长戟劲弩**。职司捕盗贼、维市序、押送囚徒；遇敌情、匪患逾百人以上，须报驻军主将，不得擅自接战。

三、关隘要冲
关隘、城门、烽燧、驿道悉归驻军专掌。城门启闭、行人勘验、烽火号次，一决于军；驿传文书由军吏监发。地方官吏不得置喙，不得于关隘别设卡口抽分。

四、反间防渗透
驻军设候奸都尉，专司稽查敌国细作。商队出入，验传（凭证）、搜夹带、录货单；来自敌境者加验关传，留滞亭舍登记。行保甲连坐：五家相保，藏谍不告者与同罪；亭长月报异客行止，匿报者坐之。

五、敌国人员限制
敌国商人、使者仅限居互市所设"客坊"，限期出入，暮鼓后不得离坊。**官府区、军营、关隘、仓廪为禁入区**；不得购置田宅、不得与本地人通婚结亲、不得充任吏役。违者没入，再犯以奸论。

六、军事触发条款
有犯下列情事之一者，朝廷得即撤销自治、改行军管：
1. 私通敌国、泄露军情关防者；
2. 擅自与敌国盟会、缔约、纳质者;
3. 窝藏敌谍、资敌粮械、为敌向导者；
4. 闭门拒守、攻击驻军、擅扩武装逾制者。

以上诸条，著为令，与自治敕书并行；敕书有与本文相抵者，以本文为准。

# The Border City Charter — 《边城互市特许状》

## Design doctrine

The entire framework rests on one maxim from the Chancellor's draft: **「财用可放，威柄不放」** — *"Wealth may be devolved; the levers of power may not."* The city receives everything it needs to function as a commercial engine, while every instrument of sovereignty (arms, law, diplomacy, coin, oversight) remains in central hands. Three problems are solved simultaneously:

| Problem | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| Economic flexibility | Delegated tariff band, commercial courts, trade regulations |
| Precedent erosion | The grant is a *personal imperial favor* issued city-by-city, explicitly barred as precedent |
| Foreign co-option | Military occupation of chokepoints, resident censors, loyalty vetting, and segregation of rival-state persons |

## I. Form of the grant — killing the precedent at birth

The autonomy is **not legislation but a grace**: issued by imperial edict, one city, one charter, bearing the inscription *"此恩止于此城，不得援例"* — "This favor ends with this city and may not be cited as precedent." Any other city petitioning on this precedent is charged with overreach, and magistrates are ordered not to receive such petitions. Because the grant flows from sovereign favor rather than law, it can be recalled by the same hand — no litigation, no appeal. It is fixed at **five years with no automatic renewal**; extension must be petitioned six months before expiry and is granted at imperial discretion.

## II. The ledger of powers

**Devolved to the city:**
- **Tariff discretion within a central band**: transit duties adjustable ±20%, market taxes ±30% around baselines set by the 治粟内史, twice yearly, filed in advance — enough agility to undercut rival markets in boom seasons and protect revenue in lean ones
- Trade regulations, market rules, merchant dispute mediation, reception of foreign caravans
- Local commercial ordinances (contracts, weights in trade, market disputes) — subject to prior filing with the 廷尉, which has 30 days to veto anything conflicting with central law

**Absolutely reserved to the center:**
- Defense and fortifications · all diplomacy with the rival power · appointment of officials · serious criminal law · coinage, weights and measures · census and conscription · salt-and-iron monopolies · control of passes, gates, beacon towers, and post roads

The city remains part of its commandery. The city head is a **centrally appointed official of county-magistrate rank — not a feudal lord, never hereditary**. A separate imperial market inspector (市监) is stationed alongside him with the right of direct memorial to the throne, so the two watch each other.

**The merchant council** is constituted as a *civil deliberative assembly* only: it may debate commerce and assist tax collection, but it receives no seals of office, may not style itself a government, and every resolution requires the city head's countersignature. Its members are entered on an official register and subject to collective liability for harboring enemy agents.

## III. Fiscal regime (治粟内史)

- **Revenue-sharing by tax type**: transit duties 70% center / 30% city; market taxes 40% / 60%; salt-iron profits entirely central (city gets 10% as escort/transport fee). Shares recalibrated every three years.
- **Double-entry ledgers**: one copy kept in the city, monthly copies to the commandery and the treasury, quarterly audits by central officials verifying goods against books.
- **Strategic-goods embargo**: weapons, armor, crossbow mechanisms, iron, grain above quota, and warhorses may never leave the pass under any exemption. Informants on smuggling receive half the confiscated value; officials who look away are punished alongside the smuggler.
- **Financial revocation triggers**: two consecutive quarters of arrears to the center; book-vs-goods divergence over 10% without explanation; shielding smugglers; taxing beyond the band or inventing new taxes; unauthorized borrowing, hoarding military supplies, or raising private troops.

## IV. Legal order (廷尉)

- **Layered law**: rebellion, treason, collaboration, violent crime, military and official law — central law exclusively. The city may legislate only on commercial matters, and never against central law.
- **Filing review**: local ordinances must be filed with the 廷尉 before taking effect; unfiled or vetoed ordinances are void, and the 廷尉 may retroactively annul.
- **Appeals**: serious criminal cases and cross-city commercial disputes ascend commandery → 廷尉, which is the final instance; capital and major cross-city cases require central review.
- **No enemy law, ever**: rival-state merchants litigate under *this* dynasty's law only; any official who adjudicates using enemy law is prosecuted as a collaborator. Senior judicial officers are appointed by the 廷尉 itself, rotated every three years.

## V. Defense and counter-intelligence (太尉)

- **The garrison answers to no one in the city**: centrally raised, under the 太尉's command, its commander imperially appointed, troops movable only against matched tallies (虎符). Council members may not enter the military camp, inspect rosters, or supervise drills — *兵权绝不假借*.
- The city may keep a police force of **at most 300 men**, wooden staves, short blades, light bows — no armor, no halberds or heavy crossbows — and may not engage any threat of over a hundred without calling the garrison.
- Passes, gates, beacon fires, and post roads are exclusively military; local officials may not set up their own checkpoints or question military movements.
- A **counter-espionage commandant (候奸都尉)** inspects caravans — permits searched, contraband searched, manifests logged; mutual-responsibility groups of five households, with concealment of spies punished as the spy; ward heads report strangers monthly.
- **Rival-state persons are quarantined**: confined to a designated trading quarter (客坊), timed entries and exits, curfew after the evening drum; barred from the government district, camps, passes, and granaries; barred from buying land or houses, marrying locals, or serving in any official capacity. Violators are confiscated; repeat offenders treated as spies.

## VI. Oversight and loyalty (御史大夫)

- **Two resident censors** at 600-dan rank, three-year non-renewable terms, subordinate to no one in the city, entitled to report on rumor alone and to **bypass the Chancellor directly to the emperor**. Any socializing between censors and local officials/merchants is itself a crime.
- **Twice-yearly loyalty vetting** of council members and all officials: suspicion of espionage, receipt of enemy gifts, marriage alliances with the enemy. Kin entering enemy territory must be pre-declared; the censor who certifies falsely is punished when discovered.
- **Asset declarations**: council members declare property and capital sources on joining and annually; unexplained enrichment is punished as bribery. Officials borrowing from council members or receiving their gifts are punished as co-corruptors.
- **Protected accusation box** in the censor's office: informants rewarded, identities kept secret, retaliation punished one degree above the original offense, false accusation punished in reverse.
- **Escorted envoys**: if the city is granted a trade envoy, a censor accompanies every border crossing; no document, gift, or agreement is valid without the censor's countersignature, and all contacts and valuables are logged and reported on return.

## VII. Infrastructure as control (少府)

Physical plant doubles as central presence: a government market with a market prefect; inns and warehouses built by the 少府 and rented out; **granaries deliberately split three ways** (military grain → central granary under a commandant; price-stabilization → commandery; trade goods → 少府). Coinage exists only as an official exchange; salt, iron, copper, and lacquer are state-supplied monopolies. Construction crews and works officers **stay garrisoned in the city** permanently — the center's hands and eyes live on site. > 朕惟王者牧民，利出一孔；驭边之道，恩威并运。丞相府会六府之议，上《边城互市特许状》，朕已省讫……其准如所奏，以诏令逐城颁授。
>

>

>
> ……夫敌国者，朕之雠也。通市者，取其利而防其奸，非亲之也……其宣示边郡，咸使闻知，如律令。

Two additions the emperor made on ratification: a **blood oath before the commandery governor** ("we shall keep the border lawfully forever, never traffic with the enemy, never accept enemy gifts, never make private alliances or exchange hostages — oath-breakers forfeit their clans"), and a **hostage-scholar system**: each leading merchant house sends its heir to the commandery academy — educated, maintained at state expense, and retained as a pledge; those who pass the law examinations are appointed officials (turning hostages into loyal cadres), violators forfeit their hostage.

## Why this works against the rival power

The rival power was promised an *opportunity* by autonomy. This framework gives it none: its merchants are quartered, curfewed, and barred from property, marriage, and office; its intelligence apparatus meets a dedicated counter-espionage commandant and collective liability; its influence-buying meets asset declarations, twice-yearly vetting, and censors with direct imperial access; its military option meets a central garrison that the city cannot command but no enemy can bribe. Meanwhile the city gets everything it actually petitioned for — tariff agility, commercial self-rule, and reduced bureaucratic drag — so the merchant council gains more by loyalty than by defection, and its leading houses' children are being educated into the imperial system itself.

- Passes, gates, beacon fires, and post roads are exclusively military; local officials may not set up their own checkpoints or question military movements.
- A **counter-espionage commandant (候奸都尉)** inspects caravans — permits searched, contraband searched, manifests logged; mutual-responsibility groups of five households, with concealment of spies punished as the spy; ward heads report strangers monthly.
- **Rival-state persons are quarantined**: confined to a designated trading quarter (客坊), timed entries and exits, curfew after the evening drum; barred from the government district, camps, passes, and granaries; barred from buying land or houses, marrying locals, or serving in any official capacity. Violators are confiscated; repeat offenders treated as spies.

## VI. Oversight and loyalty (御史大夫)

- **Two resident censors** at 600-dan rank, three-year non-renewable terms, subordinate to no one in the city, entitled to report on rumor alone and to **bypass the Chancellor directly to the emperor**. Any socializing between censors and local officials/merchants is itself a crime.
- **Twice-yearly loyalty vetting** of council members and all officials: suspicion of espionage, receipt of enemy gifts, marriage alliances with the enemy. Kin entering enemy territory must be pre-declared; the censor who certifies falsely is punished when discovered.
- **Asset declarations**: council members declare property and capital sources on joining and annually; unexplained enrichment is punished as bribery. Officials borrowing from council members or receiving their gifts are punished as co-corruptors.
- **Protected accusation box** in the censor's office: informants rewarded, identities kept secret, retaliation punished one degree above the original offense, false accusation punished in reverse.
- **Escorted envoys**: if the city is granted a trade envoy, a censor accompanies every border crossing; no document, gift, or agreement is valid without the censor's countersignature, and all contacts and valuables are logged and reported on return.

## VII. Infrastructure as control (少府)

Physical plant doubles as central presence: a government market with a market prefect; inns and warehouses built by the 少府 and rented out; **granaries deliberately split three ways** (military grain → central granary under a commandant; price-stabilization → commandery; trade goods → 少府). Weights, measures, tallies, and travel permits are **centrally manufactured, inscribed, and annually verified** — private manufacture is a crime. Coinage exists only as an official exchange; salt, iron, copper, and lacquer are state-supplied monopolies. Construction crews and works officers **stay garrisoned in the city** permanently — the center's hands and eyes live on site. Rival-state luxuries (jewels, brocades, curiosities) are heavily taxed monopolies sellable only in the official market; **gold, silver, and coin may not leave the country** — trade with the rival power is barter, so wealth flows in goods, not specie.

## VIII. Ratification — the Emperor's edict (制曰)

> 朕惟王者牧民，利出一孔；驭边之道，恩威并运。丞相府会六府之议，上《边城互市特许状》，朕已省讫……其准如所奏，以诏令逐城颁授。
>
> 然此特恩也，非通制也。一城一状，明书「此恩止于此城，不得援例」；他城援例陈请者，以僭越论，有司勿受。恩出自朕，予夺惟朕所裁，亦可随时收之。
>
> 城主简自朝廷，秩比县令，毋得世袭。到任之日，与商人议事会首户刑牲歃血，誓于郡守之前曰：「世世奉法守边，不通敌、不受敌馈、不私盟纳质。」背誓者族。首户各遣適子入郡学受业，因留为质，廪食官给；试律通者叙用，违者夺质。
>
> ……夫敌国者，朕之雠也。通市者，取其利而防其奸，非亲之也……其宣示边郡，咸使闻知，如律令。

Two additions the emperor made on ratification: a **blood oath before the commandery governor** ("we shall keep the border lawfully forever, never traffic with the enemy, never accept enemy gifts, never make private alliances or exchange hostages — oath-breakers forfeit their clans"), and a **hostage-scholar system**: each leading merchant house sends its heir to the commandery academy — educated, maintained at state expense, and retained as a pledge; those who pass the law examinations are appointed officials (turning hostages into loyal cadres), violators forfeit their hostage.

## Why this works against the rival power

The rival power was promised an *opportunity* by autonomy. This framework gives it none: its merchants are quartered, curfewed, and barred from property, marriage, and office; its intelligence apparatus meets a dedicated counter-espionage commandant and collective liability; its influence-buying meets asset declarations, twice-yearly vetting, and censors with direct imperial access; its military option meets a central garrison that the city cannot command but no enemy can bribe. Meanwhile the city gets everything it actually petitioned for — tariff agility, commercial self-rule, and reduced bureaucratic drag — so the merchant council gains more by loyalty than by defection, and its leading houses' children are being educated into the imperial system itself.
